transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Kim (Redwood AE), Lina Zhou (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (BlueNova ML), Rajesh Iyer (BlueNova Platform), Alyssa Chen (BlueNova PM)

Summary:
Quick follow-up after last weeks reliability incident — timeouts and 5xx during peak batch run. Goal: confirm root cause hypothesis, agree on mitigations (retry/backoff, rate limit tuning, batching changes), and assign next steps for pilot.

Topics: incident recap, observed error types (timeouts, 5xx gateway), rate limiting behavior, retry strategies, batching and KV cache effects, telemetry and traces, scheduling a coordinated load test.

Transcript:
00:00 Ethan: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is the weekly poc sync, main item is follow up on the incident last tuesday when you hit a spiky 5xx series during your nightly workload.
00:08 Sofia: yeah thanks Ethan, we had a big window 2am to 3am PST where about 8% of requests returned 5xx and about 15% were timeouts, it was pretty noisy and our ingest pipeline queued up, so product team freaked out.
00:20 Lina: and just to be clear, was that during batching changes you tested? I recall you increased batch size and turned on prefix cache.
00:27 Rajesh: correct, we bumped batching from 8 to 32 to save tokens and put a tiny kv cache setting, it reduced cost in general but clearly surfaced some instability.
00:35 Ethan: right, initial hypothesis from our side was an autoscaler interaction — the dedicated pool hit a transient shortage of GPUs when a high concurrency job started, so requests queued and some hit upstream timeouts. there were also a couple of 502s that looked like rpc failures.
00:47 Sofia: we saw similar traces, and we also have some nginx 504s at the edge, not sure if that was our proxy or the redwood endpoint.
00:55 Lina: the nginx 504s line up with our internal metrics for long KV lookup times; sometimes the prefix K V cache makes the initial request heavier. also the model variant you were using was the 7B quantized build which has different memory behavior.
01:05 Rajesh: fair, so is the recommendation to lower batch size or change the autoscaler?
01:10 Lina: a couple of levers. short term: enforce an application-side concurrency cap with client-side rate limit and exponential backoff so retries dont amplify the spike. medium: adjust dedicated pool autoscaler thresholds to scale earlier, and increase pod buffer. longer term: we can recommend a different quantization profile that has a smaller memory footprint under heavy prefix cache loads.
01:25 Alyssa: quick question on retries — we currently have client retry set to 3 immediate retries. that might have caused a thundering herd.
01:32 Ethan: yeah immediate retries are usually bad in spike events. Lina, can you outline the backoff pattern you recommend?
01:36 Lina: sure, aim for jittered exponential backoff starting at 200ms, cap at 3 retries with full-jitter and a randomized initial delay. also add a circuit-breaker that cuts requests when p99 latency exceeds your target for 30s.
01:51 Sofia: ok that seems reasonable; is there a recommended batch size for 7B quantized to avoid memory pressure?
01:56 Lina: for your observed seq lengths (avg 512 tokens) we suggest batch sizes between 8 and 16 for the quantized 7B. 32 is aggressive with prefix KV cache. if you bump to 16 you get decent throughput without as much memory allocation.
02:10 Rajesh: about rate limits, we saw some 429s too, unclear which side. Our infra team has an egress proxy that enforces 200 rps per IP, but the redwood client multiplexes requests over fewer connections.
02:21 Ethan: that could cause bursts that look like high per-connection rps. can you share your egress proxy config? if the proxy is pooling many requests from your worker, the per-connection limit might be tripping.
02:30 Rajesh: yeah I'll share; action item.
02:33 Lina: also, from the Redwood side we saw a small spike in queue length in the serving runtime before the 5xx window; traces show a few inbound requests with very large context windows that caused CPU stalls for the scheduling thread. could be a single outlier client stream.
02:47 Sofia: hm we did have a data collection job that sent 8k token requests, i thought we limited to 2k.
02:53 Alyssa: omg yeah that was the ETL job, it accidentally concatenated user logs.
02:57 Ethan: okay that explains part of it — big contexts plus larger batch sizes plus KV cache strain plus our autoscaler scaling slightly too slow. a multi-causal incident.
03:06 Rajesh: what about circuit breakers on the Redwood side? can you put server-side protections so a single customer stream doesnt affect the whole pool?
03:12 Lina: we have per-route queue limits and tenant-level isolation in Dedicated, but the exact thresholds are tunable. for your Dedicated pool we recommended a low-latency config that prioritizes latency over packing, which meant less headroom. we can change the route to enforce smaller per-connection batch caps and drop excessively large contexts with a 413.
03:27 Sofia: dropping large contexts is fine as long as we get clear error codes and we can retry smaller.
03:31 Ethan: agreed. we'll add explicit validation that rejects >4096 tokens with a clear message and a suggestion to chunk.
03:38 Alyssa: what artifacts will you share so we can triage? logs, traces, metrics?
03:41 Ethan: we'll share the incident logs, a short postmortem with timeline, and traces from our sampling. Lina will run a matrix of retry/backoff + batch size tests and upload a results CSV.
03:51 Lina: i'll also run a couple of controlled load tests that emulate your ETL job vs normal request mix to show the delta. i'll include p50/p95/p99 and the error breakdown.
03:58 Rajesh: and i will provide our egress proxy conf and the cron job ids that ran at 2am.
04:04 Sofia: thanks. one more question on monitoring: we want alerting thresholds, what do you recommend for p95 latency and error budget for the pilot?
04:10 Lina: recommend p95 < 350ms, p99 < 900ms, and error rate less than 1% at peak for production-like runs. for a pilot you can set p99 < 1200ms and error < 3% while tuning.
04:21 Ethan: ok i'll draft suggested pager thresholds and send to you.
04:24 Alyssa: also can we get a short runbook for actions when we see these spikes? like temporary throttles or switching to a fallback model?
04:31 Ethan: yes we'll include an ops runbook — steps to toggle batching, cap concurrency, and failover to a lower-capacity but more stable model variant.
04:38 Rajesh: what about costs if we reduce batch size or move to a different quantization profile? we need to quantify impact.
04:44 Lina: smaller batch size increases per-token cost roughly by 12-20% in your observed workload; the different quantization profile increases memory use but can reduce CPU stalls which may lower error costs — i'll include an estimated cost delta sheet.
04:58 Sofia: great. can we schedule the follow up after Lina posts the test CSV?
05:03 Ethan: yes let's target week of 2026-04-13, that gives time for tests and for BlueNova to run their integrated scenario.
05:09 Alyssa: perfect.
05:12 Ethan: quick recap and next steps: Ethan will share incident logs and a short postmortem by 2026-04-02; Lina will run retry/backoff and batching matrix and upload results by 2026-04-04; Rajesh will share egress proxy config by 2026-04-05; BlueNova will run integrated load test and share traces by 2026-04-07; we'll meet week of 2026-04-13. action items in the notes.
05:34 Sofia: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick work.
05:36 Ethan: thanks, we'll follow up in the ticket and I'll paste the postmortem into the CRM.
05:40 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-heard proper nouns and product names (eg Redwood Dedicated transcribed as redwood dedi in parts). References to KV cache and quantization sometimes split as K V cache in the transcript.
